# NSSFactory r1

_The same light, arriving sooner._

A VapourSynth factory for classical NSS (non-local self-similarity) denoisers — NLM, BM3D (+VAggregate), WNNM, MCWNNM, TWSC, NLH, NCSR, LSSC — honoring the pre-AI era of these algorithms. r1 adds a CUDA plugin that runs all eight denoisers on NVIDIA GPUs with the CPU plugin's arguments, defaults and models.

**Work in progress.** The packages below are preview builds for evaluation, not stable releases.

## Packages

| Package | Plugin | Runs on |
|---|---|---|
| `nssfactory-r1-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | `libnss.so` (`nss`) | x86-64 with AVX2; glibc 2.34 and the libstdc++ of GCC 13 (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 39 or later). Highway dynamic: AVX2 + AVX3/Zen4 |
| `nssfactory-r1-linux-arm64.tar.gz` **(new)** | `libnss.so` (`nss`) | AArch64 with glibc 2.38 (libstdc++ built in). NEON |
| `nssfactory-r1-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | `libnss.dylib` (`nss`) | Apple silicon, macOS 13.3 or newer. NEON |
| `nssfactory-r1-windows-x86_64.zip` | `libnss.dll` (`nss`) | x86-64 with AVX2 and the Visual C++ 2015–2022 Redistributable. Highway dynamic, built with clang++ (MSVC ABI) |
| `nssfactory-r1-linux-x86_64-cuda.tar.gz` **(new)** | `libnss_cuda.so` (`nss_cuda`) | as `linux-x86_64`, with an NVIDIA driver for CUDA 12.9 or newer |
| `nssfactory-r1-windows-x86_64-cuda.zip` **(new)** | `libnss_cuda.dll` (`nss_cuda`) | an NVIDIA driver for CUDA 12.9 or newer and the Visual C++ Redistributable |

Clips must be constant-format Gray/YUV/RGB 32-bit float. Each package carries `docs/api`; see the [API guide](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/README.md) for the CPU filters and the [CUDA reference](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/cuda/README.md) for the GPU ones. `core.nss.Version()` and `core.nss_cuda.Version()` report `r1`.

## Highlights

- **`nss_cuda`: every denoiser on the GPU.** Same names, arguments, defaults and models as `nss`; the output agrees with the CPU plugin to 60 dB PSNR or better (not bit for bit) and is identical from run to run on a given GPU, driver and build. 1080p YUV420 at the defaults on an RTX 5080: BM3D ~500 fps, NLM ~550, WNNM ~490, NCSR ~390, LSSC ~190, TWSC ~66, NLH ~37 (MCWNNM, RGB only: ~200). Native code for RTX 20/30/40/50 (compute capability 7.5, 8.6, 8.9, 12.0); other GPUs of 7.5 or newer through the driver's PTX JIT. `core.nss_cuda.Backend()` reports what a device gets.
- **Temporal output finished on the GPU**: with `radius > 0` the GPU filters return finished frames (`temporal_mode="rolling"`, the default); the accumulation and every outer round of MCWNNM, NCSR and TWSC stay on the device. `temporal_mode="legacy"` still returns the CPU intermediate for `core.nss.VAggregate`.
- **BM3D** gains `chroma=1` (CBM3D for YUV 4:4:4: groups matched on luma, all three planes filtered with them) and `final=1` (Basic and Wiener stages in one call), on both plugins. CPU rolling chunks now carry on from one another and run in parallel: 1080p YUV420, `radius=1`, 16 threads, **3.1 → 6.6 fps**.
- **TWSC is fast by default**: `block_step=8, group_size=8, iters=2`, plus an RGB fast color path (`cfast`, opponent planes filtered alone). The paper's quality geometry (`block_step=1, group_size=90, iters=12`) remains available and denoises 8 to 10 dB better at thousands of times the cost.
- **NLH** uses one preset for every clip (model version 6) and estimates the noise on every fourth reference.
- **New packages**: Linux arm64, and the CUDA plugin for Linux and Windows.

## Upgrading from r0

- **TWSC and NLH defaults changed** (model versions 3 → 6 and 5 → 6): their output at default arguments differs from r0. r0's TWSC default was the quality geometry above; pass it (and `cfast=0` for RGB) to get r0's geometry back. The output is still not r0's bit for bit: the models themselves moved on.
- **No CPU memory limit by default.** r0 capped each CPU filter at 1024 MB, which failed 1080p temporal BM3D on 16 threads; `memory_limit_mb` is now unset unless you give it (as on the GPU). The limit never changes the output.
- **Legacy temporal intermediates carry their model version**; `VAggregate` rejects one made by a different version, so recompute them rather than reusing r0's.
- **The Linux packages need a recent distribution** (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 39 or later); on Ubuntu 22.04 or Debian 12 the plugin fails to load with a `GLIBCXX` error. Build from source there (see `docs/api/building.md`).

## Which filter for what

Cost tiers on one CPU core (1920x1080 gray, sigma 3, defaults) and on the GPU (RTX 5080, 1080p YUV420):

| Filter | CPU ms / frame | GPU fps | Good for |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| BM3D | ~59 | ~500 | General use; the fastest |
| NLM | ~131 | ~550 | Light noise |
| WNNM | ~131 | ~490 | Texture and edge retention |
| NCSR | ~268 | ~390 | Sparse-coding quality at moderate cost |
| LSSC | ~369 | ~190 | Structured noise, film grain |
| TWSC | ~1337 | ~66 | Real-world noise; the quality geometry for the best result |
| NLH | heavy* | ~37 | Real-world noise of unknown level (blind) |
| MCWNNM | ~2326 (RGB) | ~200 (RGB) | RGB color noise |

\* NLH's blind default is much heavier than its ~6.6 s measured with given sigma and `block_size=8, block_step=8`; see its page.

- **BM3D** remains the general-purpose baseline; `chroma=1` for YUV 4:4:4 color with matching on luma, `final=1` for the two-stage result in one call.
- **NLH** — the strongest default quality in this plugin's own comparisons and blind when `sigma` is omitted; on the GPU it is now practical for whole clips.
- **TWSC** — fast by default; raise `block_step`/`group_size`/`iters` toward the paper's geometry when quality matters more than time.
- **NCSR / LSSC** — a quality tier below NLH/TWSC at much lower cost.

For usage detail, please refer to the API docs linked above.
